title: Non-overlapping intervals
statement: Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest don't overlap. Intervals are half-open in effect: [1, 2] and [2, 3] don't overlap.
hints: Equivalently, keep as many non-overlapping intervals as possible.
Among intervals compatible with what you've kept, keep the one that ends first.

solution.explanation: Maximum set of non-overlapping intervals = sort by end, take greedily. Exchange argument: in any optimal solution, replace its first interval with the earliest-ending one; nothing later conflicts, because that one ends no later. Sorting by start is the classic wrong greedy; [1, 100], [2, 3], [4, 5] breaks it. The same algorithm answers minimum arrows to burst balloons and maximum meetings in one room.
